object.definition: The nonempty compact convex set $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public and has Euclidean diameter at most $D$. The environment fixes differentiable losses before interaction. Each loss is $\mu$-strongly convex on $X$ and satisfies $$\|\nabla f_t(x)\|_2\le G,\qquad f_t(y)\ge f_t(x)+\langle\nabla f_t(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2\quad(x,y\in X).$$. Public geometric and regularity parameters must define a nonempty loss class. No minimax claim is made for incompatible strong-convexity and gradient bounds.

operation.query_signature: A causal policy chooses $x_t\in X$ and receives one exact gradient $\nabla f_t(x_t)$ there, without noise. Inputs $X,T,D,G,\mu$ are public. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.

steps: The algorithm is causal: choose $x_t\in X$ each round, then receive the sole exact gradient $\nabla f_t(x_t)$ at that point. Feedback is noiseless.
Public inputs are $X,T,D,G,\mu$. Projection computation and gradient queries are accounted for separately.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
